Definition: from G4573; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc):--devotion, that is worshipped.
BiblicalUsage: A sebasma is a thing worshipped, an object of devotion, and Paul found it in two places. At Athens he passed by and beheld their devotions, and found an altar with the inscription TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. And the man of sin exalts himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped, sitting in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that devotion is not proved by its object — Athens worshipped devoutly and ignorantly, and the man of sin will be worshipped too.
